title: Money Train
tagline: Last train of the night. Snacks for the platform.
about: Two foster brothers, both transit cops, plan to rob the train that collects subway fares.
cue: Pour drinks when Charlie sneaks aboard the money train on New Year's Eve.
faces: Our regulars from the night tour. The window table is theirs.
Puff pastry sealed around guava paste and cream cheese, brushed with sugar syrup.
Butter shortbread the size of a fare, punched through the middle, brushed with gold.
Soft, sweet spiral bun, split, pressed on the griddle with butter and buried in icing sugar.
Dark roast pulled strong with scalded milk. Sugar on the counter.
Best pastelitos on the line, and the coffee is on when the night tour lets out. Put mine on John's tab.
Lunch and drinks on the back
Thighs browned hard, then set on long-grain rice cooked slow with onion, green pepper, garlic, coriander, achiote, green olives and capers.
Roast pork, ham, Swiss, pickles and mustard, pressed flat and hot.
Pork shoulder rubbed with garlic, oregano and sour orange, roasted overnight till the skin crackles. Rice and red beans.
Thin top round simmered under a pile of onions with vinegar and garlic. White rice and tostones.
Cold lager over ice, fresh lime, tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire, chilli salt rim.
New Year's Eve is payday. Cash only.
Fresh orange juice whisked into cold sweet milk over crushed ice.
Almonds, cashews and peanuts baked with honey, sugar, cinnamon and salt, stirred till glossy. Warm in a paper cone.
Token booth nuts. The Torch stays outside.
The money train runs right under us. Charlie has plans for New Year's Eve.
Prices subject to change. No tabs, that means you, Charlie.

Never torched.How to make it300g mixed nuts2 tbsp honey1 tbsp caster sugar1/2 tsp ground cinnamon1 pinch of saltToss the nuts with the honey, sugar, cinnamon and salt until coated.Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170°C, stirring halfway.Keep stirring as they cool so they do not clump.Token cookiesButter shortbread the size of a fare, punched through the middle, brushed with gold.Good for a cookie. Not a ride.How to make it200g soft butter100g icing sugar300g plain flour1 small jar edible gold dustBeat the butter and icing sugar until pale, then mix in the flour to a soft dough.Chill the dough for 15 minutes so it rolls cleanly.Roll 5mm thick, cut rounds the size of a subway token and cut a small hole from the middle of each.Bake at 160°C until just set and pale gold.Cool on the tray, then brush with gold dust mixed with a drop of water.MainsArroz con polloThighs browned hard, then set on long-grain rice cooked slow with onion, green pepper, garlic, coriander, achiote, green olives and capers.Big enough for two brothers.How to make it800g chicken thighs1 brown onion, diced1 capsicum, diced3 garlic cloves, crushed1 handful coriander, chopped1 tsp ground annatto300g long grain rice60g green olives1 tbsp capers650ml chicken stock2 tbsp oil for browningBrown the chicken in the oil in a wide lidded pan until golden, then set aside.Fry the onion, capsicum, garlic and coriander in the same pan until soft.Stir in the annatto, rice, olives, capers and stock and bring to a simmer.Sit the chicken on top, cover and cook on low until the rice is tender.Rest, covered, before serving.SweetsPastelitos de guayabaPuff pastry sealed around guava paste and cream cheese, brushed with sugar syrup.Out of the oven every hour till close.How to make it2 sheets of puff pastry250g guava paste150g cream cheese3 tbsp caster sugar3 tbsp waterThaw the pastry, then cut each sheet into 8 squares.Put a slice of guava paste and a little cream cheese on half the squares, cover with the rest and seal the edges with a fork.Bake at 200°C until puffed and golden.Simmer the sugar with the water for a few minutes to make a syrup, then brush it over the warm pastries.DrinksPayday micheladaCold lager over ice, fresh lime, tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire, chilli salt rim.Friday is payday. Cash only.How to make it1 tbsp flaky salt1 tsp chilli powder5 limes, juiced, with some cut into wedges240ml tomato juice16 dashes of hot sauce8 dashes of Worcestershire sauce4 bottles of cold lager, 375ml each1 bag iceMix the salt and chilli powder on a plate.Rub a lime wedge around each of 4 glass rims and dip in the chilli salt.Add ice a good squeeze of lime juice, the tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire, dividing evenly.Top each with a cold lager, stir gently and slip the glasses into small paper bags.
